note: The printed body with the declared expansion of its Per Dóminum cue. The exact digital reading differs in two consonantal j spellings, one capital and two commas.

adjudicated.ruling: Witness do prints consonantal j; the Benziger Brothers 1962 Editio iuxta typicam page, printed p. 467, leaf n548, prints i, and the edition follows it (ORTHOGRAPHY rule 2).

Witness do prints consonantal j; the Benziger Brothers 1962 Editio iuxta typicam prints Iesum in Rubricae generales 115 a, p. xvii, leaf n22, which supplies this conclusion, and the edition follows it (ORTHOGRAPHY rule 2).
Witness do has a comma after Christum; the Missal prints the full conclusion without it (pp. 123, 365, 389, 539, 646), and the declared expansion follows that form.
The declared house expansion begins the relative clause with Qui, as the Missal prints the full conclusion; the pinned digital formula has lowercase qui. The word is unchanged.
Rubricae generales 115 a prints Sancti, Deus with a comma, and the declared expansion keeps it; the pinned digital formula has none. The words are unchanged.
